one_line: A bounded DAX learning mission where an agent coaches without owning learner evidence.
what_it_does: Provides structured, state-aware DAX guidance while keeping attempts, evaluation, and mastery under learner control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to live learner context and bounded coaching actions, while preserving an authority boundary that UI-driving automation would handle less reliably.
leverage_evidence: About text describes live learner state, Filter Trace, Explanation, and Socratic guidance selected through WebMCP.
Frame sheets show active implementation and changing product/application states.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent evidence-driven learning loop and the video shows substantial tool-driven execution, though the final learner-facing flow is not cleanly presented in every frame.
execution_evidence: About text reports 12/12 exercises, 8/8 skills, and a completed transfer challenge.
Video frames show code, consoles, and application-state progression.
impact_rationale: DAX learners have a concrete conceptual problem, and bounded assistance that cannot counterfeit mastery is a credible educational benefit.
impact_evidence: DAX filter context and CALCULATE are a specific learning need.
The design separates assistance from evaluated evidence.
creativity_rationale: The human/agent learning contract and evidence-preserving tutoring model are a fresh, thoughtfully pursued angle on AI education.
creativity_evidence: Agent helps but cannot become the learner.
Socratic and state-aware guidance are integrated into a deterministic mission.
usability_note: Clear learning loop and authority boundary; dense technical presentation may raise onboarding cost.
red_flags: Final end-to-end learner experience is less clearly shown than implementation activity.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP rationale, credible educational value, and substantial execution evidence.

one_line: A shared human-agent desk for reviewing hospital bills before payment.
what_it_does: Loads itemized bills, flags billing anomalies, requires line-by-line review, and locks a hold with a call script.
leverage_rationale: Structured access ties agent findings to exact bill lines and shared review state; a general agent's prose would leave the user to remap advice manually.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly contrasts shared line-item review with a paragraph from a chatbot.
Frames show a coherent bill-review interface with findings and marked lines.
execution_rationale: The described workflow is unusually complete for scope, from import through deterministic checks, review gating, hold locking, and call-script generation; video shows the product consistently.
execution_evidence: About text lists import, statuses, five billing-shape checks, review gating, and Lock hold.
Frame sheets show repeated bill and findings states.
impact_rationale: Patients and families face a real, costly, confusing problem, and the product directly supports an actionable pre-payment review.
impact_evidence: Specific audience: people receiving itemized hospital bills.
Output is actionable: flagged lines, amount held, and billing-office call script.
creativity_rationale: The shared bill-review desk is a strong practical synthesis with a meaningful human-agent authority model, though the underlying category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent inspect the same live statement.
Deterministic billing-shape checks are embedded in the workflow.
usability_note: The review states, hold lock, and call script make the workflow concrete and actionable.
red_flags: Video does not visibly prove agent tool invocation.
standouts: Actionable line-level review and hold workflow
advance_reason: Best combination of concrete user need, WebMCP state delta, and coherent product scope.

one_line: A browser 3D previz editor where agents help turn directing intent into camera motion.
what_it_does: Stages characters and cameras, creates keyframes and annotations, previews shots, and lets an agent plan and validate trajectories.
leverage_rationale: Structured scene inspection and precise trajectory calculation are substantially more reliable than driving a complex 3D editor through pixels.
leverage_evidence: About text describes complete scene inspection, shot planning, trajectory calculation, validation, and writes back to the editor.
Frames show technical visualization and changing outputs.
execution_rationale: The scope is ambitious and the packet shows visible visualization/output progression, but the central human-to-agent-to-final-shot workflow is not demonstrated cleanly end to end.
execution_evidence: About text enumerates editor, timeline, camera preview, import/save/export features.
Frame sheets show repeated chart/visualization and application states.
impact_rationale: Directors and previs artists have a real iteration bottleneck in translating intent into blocking and camera paths; the proposed workflow addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Specific film-previsualization workflow is described.
Agent handles calculation while director retains creative direction.
creativity_rationale: Natural-language directing paired with validated 3D blocking is a fresh and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Continuous-shot example with reveal/hide choreography.
World-space and camera-space annotations plus agent validation.
usability_note: Powerful but technically dense 3D workflow; director-facing polish is not fully evidenced.
red_flags: Video evidence is engineering-oriented and does not clearly prove a complete shot workflow.
advance_reason: High ambition and meaningful structured-state leverage with credible, if incomplete, execution evidence.

one_line: An evidence-first Swedish election research layer that exposes sources and gaps to agents.
what_it_does: Presents party claims with quotes, dates, cost ranges, source links, archive copies, and human verification rather than automated verdicts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured published evidence and visible gaps directly to an agent, reducing hallucination and source-mapping risk in a high-stakes research task.
leverage_evidence: About text says WebMCP exposes published sources, visible gaps, and human-in-the-loop verification.
Frames show comparison cards, source-oriented pages, and result states.
execution_rationale: The product story, evidence cards, and comparison flow are coherent and visibly demonstrated, though factual correctness cannot be verified from frames.
execution_evidence: About text reports evidence records with Swedish quotes, publication dates, cost ranges, links, and archive copies.
Video shows comparison and evidence-result states.
impact_rationale: Voters, especially first-time voters, have a real need for sourced and uncertainty-aware election information; the product addresses it without substituting a political verdict.
impact_evidence: Specific Swedish election audience and 2026 use case.
Evidence-not-verdict and human verification framing.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-native evidence access, visible gaps, and non-partisan human verification is an original and socially meaningful interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Recorded unclear positions instead of filling gaps.
Evidence layer explicitly separates sourcing from recommendation.
usability_note: Evidence-rich and reviewable, though information density may challenge casual voters.
red_flags: Source accuracy and coverage are not independently verifiable from packet evidence.
advance_reason: High impact and a clear, safety-conscious WebMCP role.

one_line: An adaptive micro-step interface where a person and agent shape a manageable path together.
what_it_does: Turns overwhelming goals into accepted micro-steps, uses friction signals to propose smaller replacements, and preserves visible progress and undo.
leverage_rationale: The agent reads structured goal, path, friction, progress, and undo state and proposes changes without silently accepting them; pixel-driving would be fragile and unsafe.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies five bounded tools and the authority boundary.
Frames show a consistent adaptive goal flow and progress states.
execution_rationale: The workflow has clear states, acceptance boundaries, friction feedback, progress, and undo; the video shows a coherent polished interface, though agent invocation is not visible.
execution_evidence: About text gives concrete before/after micro-step example and 1-of-5 progress.
Frame sheets show multiple coherent mobile product states.
impact_rationale: People facing unemployment or cognitively overwhelming goals have a real need for smaller actionable next steps, and the product directly supports agency.
impact_evidence: Example user context: losing a job and not knowing where to start.
Friction becomes an explicit signal rather than a silent failure.
creativity_rationale: Treating overwhelm as a structured interaction signal and requiring human acceptance of agent proposals is a distinctive collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: This feels like too much produces a smaller replacement.
Agent proposes while person remains responsible for acceptance.
usability_note: Calm, legible micro-step and undo flow is highly approachable.
red_flags: Video does not visibly prove agent invocation despite strong written protocol.
advance_reason: Strong product coherence and a meaningful, carefully bounded agent role.

one_line: A playable browser game editor that lets creators prompt an agent, run the change, and play again.
what_it_does: Connects a KAPLAYGROUND-based editor to WebMCP so an agent can inspect, edit, run, and check a game while the creator directs and tests it.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes the edit-run-feedback loop more reliable than manually translating prompts into code and navigating an editor, but competent agents can approximate much of it through general tools.
leverage_evidence: About text describes open-project awareness, editing, running, and useful checks.
Frames visibly combine running game output with editor/code states.
execution_rationale: The central play-prompt-replay loop is visibly real and the packet honestly identifies the existing KAPLAYGROUND foundation; the scope is coherent.
execution_evidence: About text reports a working demo where the assistant changes the character to Bobo and the result is played.
Frame sheets show game output alongside development panels.
impact_rationale: Beginner and experimental game creators can reach a playable result without setting up a local development environment, making the use case accessible and concrete.
impact_evidence: Specific creator workflow starts from a working browser game.
People can also play, edit manually, save, and export portable copies.
creativity_rationale: Prompting changes to a live playable game and immediately testing them is a memorable creative loop, even though it extends an existing editor.
creativity_evidence: Play-prompt-replay interaction model.
Agent edits are bounded by run feedback and creator testing.
usability_note: Immediate play feedback lowers the barrier to experimentation; editor density may still challenge novices.
red_flags: Built on pre-existing KAPLAYGROUND; challenge contribution is the WebMCP workflow rather than the underlying editor.
advance_reason: Strong demonstrated workflow and creative interaction, with moderate rather than transformative WebMCP delta.

one_line: A WebMCP page where an agent animates a measured rigged 3D character from natural language.
what_it_does: Describes a loaded figure, sets poses and joint angles, checks motion, and renders animation through structured tools.
leverage_rationale: The agent receives measured figure geometry, bone roles, units, prior motion, and verification feedback, making reliable natural-language animation substantially more practical than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text says 20 tools report measured model data and solver miss distances.
Frames show explicit Blender/tool workflow, character poses, and animation output.
execution_rationale: The video clearly shows tool-driven character animation and rendered/preview output; the scope is focused and coherent, though some frames are intermediate previews.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show Blender-like controls, scene views, altered poses, and output.
About text specifies pose, joint, checking, and rendering tools.
impact_rationale: Independent creators and agent developers can obtain usable character motion without animation software or rig setup, addressing a real technical barrier.
impact_evidence: Product removes rig setup and exposes figure-specific measurements.
Natural-language animation and downloadable clip are explicit goals.
creativity_rationale: The measured, self-aware rig plus same-prompt Blender/WebMCP comparison is a novel and ambitious way to make agent animation reliable.
creativity_evidence: Backflip challenge tests physical plausibility.
Same-agent, same-prompt comparison isolates the interaction surface.
usability_note: Natural-language control is approachable, while 3D animation output remains technically demanding.
red_flags: Some output appears preview-level rather than fully production-rendered.
advance_reason: One of the clearest demonstrations of WebMCP changing what an agent can reliably do.

one_line: A 3D mystery escape room designed to benchmark agents through constrained WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Lets agents explore, inspect, collect evidence, unlock rooms, derive codes, submit a supported theory, and escape.
leverage_rationale: The product is built around structured, legitimate observations and actions in a shared world; generic UI driving would be less repeatable and less auditable as a benchmark.
leverage_evidence: About text lists 21 tools spanning observation, movement, evidence, and solution submission.
Frames show changing rooms, puzzle states, and tool-driven progression.
execution_rationale: The deterministic mystery engine, five interconnected locations, and visible progression indicate a substantial coherent benchmark/game, although final escape success is not unambiguously shown.
execution_evidence: About text describes a complete mission loop and tools exposing only legitimately knowable information.
Frame sheets show multiple room and puzzle states.
impact_rationale: Agent developers and evaluators have a concrete need for interactive, repeatable tests of investigation, tool use, and evidence-based reasoning.
impact_evidence: Explicit benchmark purpose beyond text or coding tests.
Rankings and agent report cards are described in the packet.
creativity_rationale: A navigable 3D mystery with evidence-linked reasoning and a verified end state is a memorable, ambitious benchmark interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Five-location missing-researcher mystery.
Agent must connect clues across locations and submit a supported theory.
usability_note: The mission is compelling but complex; onboarding and benchmark interpretation may require explanation.
red_flags: Video does not clearly prove a successful final escape or report-card completion.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated and WebMCP-central, with strong visible interactive execution.

one_line: A semantic application-state reproduction tool that renders the real UI for a chosen state.
what_it_does: Discovers application states, reproduces them in an isolated session, and lets humans or agents inspect production-like UI without real side effects.
leverage_rationale: Semantic state discovery and reproduction give agents stable state-level control that is materially more reliable than navigating or mutating an app through pixels.
leverage_evidence: About text describes list_states, reproduce_state, and reset_state as stable tools.
Frames show reproduction documentation and terminal/package execution.
execution_rationale: The package workflow and command-line evidence make the concept plausible and technically specific, but the video emphasizes documentation and setup more than a clean reproduced UI end state.
execution_evidence: About text gives npm install, scan, setup, isolated session, and state-source workflow.
Frame sheet includes terminal commands and reproduction report views.
impact_rationale: Developers and QA teams have a real recurring cost in recreating expired, unauthenticated, error, and subscription states; safe isolated reproduction directly reduces it.
impact_evidence: Specific application-testing pain points are enumerated.
Avoids real users, payments, emails, and production side effects.
creativity_rationale: Treating semantic UI states as discoverable, reproducible data is an original and useful agent-native testing abstraction.
creativity_evidence: Static analysis discovers states from branches, enums, mocks, fixtures, and tests.
One generic bridge replaces many bespoke test tools.
usability_note: Powerful for developers, but integration and supported state architectures may be technically demanding.
red_flags: Clean end-user reproduction result is not prominently demonstrated in video frames.
advance_reason: High developer value and a meaningful structured-state delta, with execution confidence reduced by thin final-result evidence.

one_line: A connected canvas where people and agents turn ideas into plans, traces, and learning maps.
what_it_does: Maintains shared visual context for build, trace, and learn maps with nodes, evidence, comments, delivery status, and human-controlled locks.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets an agent read selection and workspace context and create linked structures directly on the shared canvas, avoiding lossy copy-paste from chat.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 15 tools for reading context, creating maps, updating plans, adding evidence, and focusing paths.
Frames show consistent purple notebook/workspace states and dialogs.
execution_rationale: The product has a coherent multi-map model, inspector, evidence, locks, and learning quiz; video shows a stable visual workspace across states, though the definitive end state is somewhat ambiguous.
execution_evidence: About text specifies build, trace, and learn maps plus inspector and locks.
Frame sheets show multiple connected workspace views and interaction states.
impact_rationale: Teams, researchers, learners, and individual planners have a real problem of losing relationships and context in chat; a shared canvas credibly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific use cases include product roadmaps, system traces, and learning maps.
Evidence, delivery status, comments, and locks keep work reviewable.
creativity_rationale: Combining planning, tracing, and learning as connected agent-readable maps is a fresh synthesis with a thoughtful human-control layer.
creativity_evidence: Person selects a node and asks the agent to generate a related trace.
Human-controlled locks preserve important decisions.
usability_note: Shared visual context is compelling, though many map types and inspector features add complexity.
red_flags: The video is dense and does not isolate one complete workflow as clearly as the written description.
advance_reason: Coherent shared-workspace product with strong WebMCP rationale and credible visible execution.
